html:
The Karuwali are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Channel Country of southwest Queensland. On the map their lands lie west of today's Windorah, beside those of the Birria, Mithaka and Yarluyandi.

Little is written about them. Their neighbours lived in a land of braided, mostly dry channels that flood after rain far to the north. People camped by lasting waterholes, hunted, and ground grass seed and nardoo into flour. Cattle stations spread through the region in the 1870s and took over the waterholes.
